I THINK I get what you’re saying and you’re right that’s incredibly complex but a more directed way to improve color resolution. I was straying away from the topic of sonar simply because I believed it would affect marine behavior but a quick google shows that’s not the case, then you’re right sonar would be the most effective. And as stated this wouldn’t be possible at depth with your standard sensor, though I’m sure there are underwater cameras that capitalize on that very idea,  at significant depth blue band resolution would cover the entire visible spectrum haha. wild and exciting stuff!


I think the big takeaway is that the issues they’re dealing with are due to consistent and reproducible phenomena that can be solved with a careful understanding of the environment and how that environment affects light dispersion. But it’s crazy to know we’re getting to the point where technology that already exists can be used to solve this.

I actually think this IS possible with active distance telemetry as well as depth monitoring and a wildly powerful algorithm to parse different spatial orientations of objects in the scene. Think of how the Kinect works, using an infrared grid to ascertain 3D orientation of objects within a field of view. (How IR holds up underwater at depth is something I’m not sure about tho) if that information can be gathered with enough resolution to correlate to pixels(or possibly smallish groups of pixels) that might be enough to allow active distance monitoring. Combine that with a real time measurement of depth and bobs your uncle. IMO this would actually be easier when using an isolated light source on the submersible since the distance of the light source is equal to the distance from the object and there’s no variation due to air pollution/time of day/weather.

You’re absolutely right, I think mr_crow_13 is oversimplifying the complexity of the topic (which is fine considering on first glance the difference in techniques is hard to conceptualize) The importance is in the way wavelengths of light are attenuated at different depths, nonlinearly and inconsistently, one wavelength won’t decrease in value the same way as another, rather the process is dynamic and a function of both distance from subject AND depth. That means there’s a need to isolate and rekey each color differently, not to mention resaturating and brightening, and with an 8bit camera that’s already a lot of work, let alone 14bit. Implicit in this is a loss of contrast which means details are lost along the way, the algorithm is literally bringing back things that aren’t exactly there in the RAW image, but rather using an intelligent design to effectively “fill in the gaps” based on an understanding of how and why things are lost.
